claims.text: The base (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a robust field-induced caloric response.
The base alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack under applied loads.
Adding approximately 0.5 at% boron and homogenizing at approximately 800°C for 2 hours will promote boron segregation to grain boundaries.
The segregated boron will form a thin, cohesive intergranular film.
Boron segregation will reduce grain-boundary energy.
The boron-rich grain-boundary film will improve intergranular cohesion.
The boron-rich film will retard crack initiation and propagation.
The boron treatment will not significantly alter the bulk crystallographic structure.
The boron treatment will preserve the martensitic transformation responsible for the caloric response.
The treated alloy will achieve a compressive strength exceeding approximately 300 MPa.
The treated alloy will exhibit less than a 10% decrease in caloric entropy change relative to the unchanged alloy.
Epoxy-containing comparator materials have reported compressive strengths of 152–218 MPa.
The original unchanged alloy has a compressive strength of 152–218 MPa.

The intervention will remain effective under magnetic fields of approximately 2 T, pressures of approximately 200 MPa, near-room-temperature cycling around the martensitic transition, and mechanical loads up to approximately 300 MPa.
Minor boron additions may produce thicker films or continuous boride phases.
Formation of thicker films or continuous boride phases may alter the martensitic transformation and impair caloric performance.

contradictions.description: The baseline attributes the 152–218 MPa compressive-strength range to the original alloy, whereas the predicted-outcome field attributes that same range to epoxy composites.

The predicted strength target is greater than approximately 300 MPa, but the falsification rule only requires a 30% improvement over the control. Depending on control strength, a result below 300 MPa could violate the stated target without falsifying the hypothesis.
